subproblem.title: Restricted representing integrals are determined by the represented current
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. For i = 1, 2, 3 let μ_i be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ_i(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and ξ_i : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k, continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm) for μ_i-a.e. x and every k-covector α. If ∫ ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫ ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ + ∫ ξ₃(x)(ω(x)) dμ₃ for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), then for every Borel set B ⊆ ℝ^P and every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U): ∫_B ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫_B ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ + ∫_B ξ₃(x)(ω(x)) dμ₃.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ₁ μ₂ μ₃ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ₁ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ₂ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ₃ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₁ μ₁ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₂ μ₂ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₃ μ₃ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₁, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₁ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₂, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₂ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₃, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₃ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, ∫ x, ξ₁ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, ξ₂ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₂ + ∫ x, ξ₃ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₃) → ∀ (B : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U k), MeasurableSet B → ∫ x in B, ξ₁ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₁ = ∫ x in B, ξ₂ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₂ + ∫ x in B, ξ₃ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₃
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the "Consequences" paragraph of the parent's (REP) notes and V4(o) of the parent proof (coordinatewise, a finite signed Radon measure annihilating C_c^∞ is zero). Notation: |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a k-covector, ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a test form ω, and ξ_i(ω) denotes x ↦ ξ_i(x)(ω(x)).

1. Integrability. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and C := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U; ‖ω‖_∞ < ∞ since ω is continuous with compact support. For each i, x ↦ ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable (ξ_i is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable, ω is continuous and the evaluation map (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) is continuous), and for μ_i-a.e. x, |ξ_i(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ 1_C(x). Since μ_i(C) < ∞, ξ_i(ω) and ψ·ξ_i(ω) are μ_i-integrable for every bounded Borel ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ; in particular all integrals in the statement (over ℝ^P or over a Borel set B) are finite and well defined.

2. Coefficients. The space Λ^k of k-covectors on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) k) is finite-dimensional. If it is {0} (this happens exactly when k > P, since an alternating k-linear map vanishes on k linearly dependent vectors, Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent) then ω = 0, all integrands vanish and the conclusion reads 0 = 0 + 0. Otherwise fix a basis (β_I)_{I ∈ ℐ} of Λ^k with dual coordinate functionals c_I (continuous linear maps Λ^k → ℝ). For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) put ω_I := c_I ∘ ω; ω_I is C^∞ with tsupport ω_I ⊆ tsupport ω, a compact subset of U, and ω(x) = Σ_I ω_I(x) β_I. Put g_{i,I}(x) := ξ_i(x)(β_I); it is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable with |g_{i,I}| ≤ |β_I| μ_i-a.e., and ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) g_{i,I}(x) by linearity of ξ_i(x). Replacing each g_{i,I} by a Borel function equal to it μ_i-a.e. (and bounded by |β_I|) changes none of the integrals below, so we may and do assume the g_{i,I} are Borel.

3. Test identities. For I ∈ ℐ and φ ∈ C_c^∞(U) (smooth, compact support inside U), the form φβ_I belongs to 𝒟^k(U), and the hypothesis applied to it gives
   ∫ φ g_{1,I} dμ₁ = ∫ φ g_{2,I} dμ₂ + ∫ φ g_{3,I} dμ₃.   (∗)

4. A signed measure. Fix I ∈ ℐ and ψ ∈ C_c^∞(U) and let S := tsupport ψ (compact ⊆ U). The functions h_i := ψ g_{i,I} are bounded by ‖ψ‖_∞|β_I| 1_S μ_i-a.e., so the two finite Borel measures
   ν₊ := (h₁)⁺μ₁ + (h₂)⁻μ₂ + (h₃)⁻μ₃,   ν₋ := (h₁)⁻μ₁ + (h₂)⁺μ₂ + (h₃)⁺μ₃
(withDensity measures; total masses ≤ ‖ψ‖_∞|β_I|(μ₁(S) + μ₂(S) + μ₃(S)) < ∞) satisfy ∫ φ dν₊ − ∫ φ dν₋ = ∫ φψ g_{1,I} dμ₁ − ∫ φψ g_{2,I} dμ₂ − ∫ φψ g_{3,I} dμ₃ for bounded Borel φ. For φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) the product φψ lies in C_c^∞(U), hence by (∗) ∫ φ dν₊ = ∫ φ dν₋ for all φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P).

5. Two finite Borel measures ν₊, ν₋ on ℝ^P with ∫ φ dν₊ = ∫ φ dν₋ for all φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) are equal. (a) For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) the mollifications φ_ε := φ ∗ ρ_ε are in C_c^∞(ℝ^P), satisfy |φ_ε| ≤ ‖φ‖_∞ and φ_ε → φ uniformly; dominated convergence for the finite measures ν_± gives ∫ φ dν₊ = ∫ φ dν₋. (b) For a compact set K choose φ_m ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1, φ_m = 1 on K and φ_m = 0 outside {dist(·, K) < 1/m}; then φ_m ↓ 1_K pointwise and dominated convergence gives ν₊(K) = ν₋(K). (c) Compact sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (every closed set is a countable union of compact sets), and ν₊(ℝ^P) = lim_m ν₊(B̄_m(0)) = lim_m ν₋(B̄_m(0)) = ν₋(ℝ^P) < ∞; by uniqueness of finite measures agreeing on a generating π-system (Mathlib MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite), ν₊ = ν₋.

6. Conclusion. Let B be Borel and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). For each I apply steps 4–5 with ψ := ω_I and evaluate ν₊(B) = ν₋(B): ∫_B ω_I g_{1,I} dμ₁ = ∫_B ω_I g_{2,I} dμ₂ + ∫_B ω_I g_{3,I} dμ₃ (all integrals finite by step 1). Summing over the finitely many I ∈ ℐ and using ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) g_{i,I}(x) (step 2) yields ∫_B ξ₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫_B ξ₂(ω) dμ₂ + ∫_B ξ₃(ω) dμ₃. ∎
proof_key_steps: All integrands are integrable: |ξ_i(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω} a.e. and μ_i(tsupport ω) < ∞.
Expand ω in a basis β_I of k-covectors: ξ_i(ω) = Σ_I ω_I g_{i,I} with g_{i,I} := ξ_i(β_I); the case Λ^k = 0 (k > P) is trivial.
Testing the hypothesis with φβ_I, φ ∈ C_c^∞(U), gives ∫φ g_{1,I}dμ₁ = ∫φ g_{2,I}dμ₂ + ∫φ g_{3,I}dμ₃.
For ψ ∈ C_c^∞(U) the finite measures ν_± built from the positive/negative parts of ψg_{i,I} have equal integrals against C_c^∞(ℝ^P).
Mollification, approximation of indicators of compact sets and uniqueness on the π-system of compact sets give ν₊ = ν₋.
Evaluate at B with ψ := ω_I and sum over I.

audit.reason: The proposition matches every representation and measurability hypothesis. Compact-support integrability, coefficient expansion, uniqueness of finite measures against smooth tests, and evaluation on Borel restrictions prove the exact conclusion without circularity.
